messages:
customer_acme_platform: Hey team — since we switched our Redwood integration to use PrivateLink yesterday, our production service sees intermittent 502s and very high tail latency (p95/p99). Only traffic from our VPC to the vpce endpoint is affected, public traffic to the hosted API is fine. This started right after we created the interface endpoint + added the conditional egress allowlist for outbound TLS. Can you help?

carl_support: Sorry about that — we'll get this triaged. Quick Qs: 1) Is the VPCE an interface endpoint (ENIs) or an NLB-based endpoint? 2) Any recent NLB/ALB changes? 3) Can you reproduce with curl and dig from an affected host?

customer_acme_platform: It's an interface endpoint (com.amazonaws.vpce-svc-xxxx). We did roll a new NLB for internal routing last week (for canary). Repro below from an app pod: 

```
$ curl -v --resolve "api.redwood.customer:443:10.10.5.12" https://api.redwood.customer/health -w "\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code} TIME_TOTAL:%{time_total}\n" 
* Connected to api.redwood.customer (10.10.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake completed (protocol TLSv1.2)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.customer
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
> Accept: */*\n
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\n
HTTP_CODE:502 TIME_TOTAL:1.642
```

And a dig: 
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.customer
vpce-1234-resolver-abcdef.vpce-svc.amazonaws.com.
```

anya_neteng: Thanks — two things jump out: 1) split-horizon PHZ (private hosted zone) can return the resolver CNAME which is normal, but we need to ensure the endpoint's security groups + route table allow the ENIs to reach the NLB/targets. 2) 502 + TLS hints at SNI or ALPN mismatch when the NLB/ALB is terminating TLS or proxying. Can you share the endpoint's SGs and the target group's type (IP vs instance)?

customer_acme_platform: Target group is IP targets (pods on EKS). SGs: vpce-sg allows 443 outbound, targets' sg allow 443 from vpce-sg. Route table for the subnet with ENIs points to the default route via TGW/IGW depending on AZ — not doing NAT for inside traffic.

mason_sre: Quick repro step: can you tcpdump a failed handshake between the pod and the pod-target IP? Look for ClientHello SNI and server certificate. Example tcpdump: 
```
sudo tcpdump -nn -i eth0 host 10.10.5.12 and port 443 -w /tmp/vpce.pcap
```

customer_acme_platform: Uploaded pcap to the ticket. Snippet from tshark: 
```
TLSv1.2 Record Layer: Handshake Protocol: Client Hello (SNI: api.redwood.customer)
TLSv1.2 Record Layer: Handshake Protocol: Server Hello
Alert (Level: Fatal, Description: handshake_failure)
```

anya_neteng: That confirms server rejecting handshake. Two possible causes: A) NLB/ALB is doing TLS passthrough but the target expects different SNI (hostname mismatch) B) intermediate proxy rewrites SNI or terminates TLS with a cert that doesn't include the requested name. Do your targets present a cert for api.redwood.customer?

customer_acme_platform: Targets present a cert for api.redwood.customer (we validated on direct path). But direct path (skipping VPCE) works. Only when routed through vpce->NLB->targets it fails.

carl_support: Another common gotcha: interface endpoints in a VPC can route traffic back through TGW or an egress proxy if route tables prefer a centralized egress. That can cause hairpin or asymmetric routing where reply packets don't reach the ENI source IP, breaking TLS. Can you share `ip route get` from the pod node to the target IP?

customer_acme_platform: From the node: 

```
$ ip route get 10.10.201.22
10.10.201.22 via 10.10.0.1 dev eth0 src 10.10.5.12 uid 0
    cache
```

anya_neteng: Looks OK at node level. Ask: are any NACLs or firewalls doing TCP reset on long-lived TLS connections? Also is there a proxy in path (Envoy sidecar) on the targets that enforces SNI?

customer_acme_platform: We do have an Envoy sidecar. Staging (same config) works. Production traffic hits 502s after ~1.2s. We captured envoy logs showing: `upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers`

mason_sre: That log often means upstream closed the connection immediately (RST) or refused. Could be because source IP is the VPCE ENI vs node IP and upstream has an allowlist expecting node cidr. Check target pod's iptables/iptables rules and envoy listener binding.

infra-bot: ci/cd: deployed nlb-internal-canary v2 -> 2023-11-17T11:23:02Z (metadata: proxy-protocol:enabled)

anya_neteng: Ah — infra-bot shows proxy-protocol enabled on NLB. If proxy-protocol is enabled but targets are IP targets without proxy-proxy support (or Envoy not configured to accept proxy-protocol), the TCP payload will be corrupt (proxy header prepended) and TLS handshake will fail -> handshake_failure. That fits the symptoms (works direct, fails via NLB with proxy protocol).

customer_acme_platform: We didn't realize proxy-protocol was on. How do we verify?

mason_sre: Two ways: 1) check NLB attributes in AWS console/CLI: `aws elbv2 describe-load-balancer-attributes --load-balancer-arn <arn>` and look for `proxy_protocol_v2.enabled`. 2) tcpdump raw bytes on target port and look for `PROXY` header before TLS ClientHello.

customer_acme_platform: Ran describe -> shows `proxy_protocol_v2.enabled = true`. tcpdump snippet indeed shows a `PROXY TCP4` header before the TLS record. 

carl_support: Root cause identified: NLB configured with proxy protocol v2, but Envoy on targets isn't accepting proxy headers. When proxy protocol is enabled, the load balancer injects a header that the server must understand; otherwise the TLS handshake parsing fails.

anya_neteng: Remediation options: 
- Turn off proxy-protocol on the NLB (quickest) OR
- Enable proxy-protocol support on the target (Envoy: `use_proxy_proto: true` on the listener) OR
- Switch target group to instances and use a host-level proxy that understands proxy-protocol.

customer_acme_platform: We turned proxy-protocol off as a quick test and issue went away immediately (no more 502s, latency back to normal). We'll coordinate a proper rollout to support proxy-protocol in Envoy for metrics.

carl_support: Great — closing the immediate incident. Follow-ups: 1) add a check in deploy pipeline to flag proxy-protocol toggles (infra-bot note) 2) we recommend documenting VPCE + NLB proxy-protocol compatibility for customers (I'll open a doc PR). 3) Eng-RT / net to review if any Redwood endpoints are rolled with proxy-protocol by default. Tagging eng-rt for visibility.

eng-rt: Acknowledged. We'll audit recent NLB changes and add a quick diff to infra CI that prevents enabling proxy-protocol on interface-endpoint-backed target groups without a validated config on targets.

customer_acme_platform: Thanks all — we'll follow up on the Envoy changes and let you know when ready to re-enable proxy-protocol for internal observability.

mason_sre: Notes for ticket: root cause: proxy-protocol header inserted by internal NLB; symptom: TLS handshake_failure -> 502; repro: tcpdump shows `PROXY` prefix; mitigation: disable proxy-protocol or enable proxy handling on Envoy. Owner: customer infra + eng-rt for infra hardening.

carl_support: Marking this thread resolved for now. Please reopen if anything recurs. :white_check_mark:
